SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: The source of أفعلت is always إفعال; the verse’s يخرجكم إخراجا exemplifies this pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: فالمصدر على أفعلت إفعالا أبدا وذلك قولك أعطيت إعطاء وأخرجت إخراجا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: افتعلت forms its verbal noun on افتعال, with the initial alif connected, as in احتبست احتباسا and انطلقت انطلاقا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: وأما افتعلت فمصدره عليه افتعالا وألفه موصولة كما كانت موصولة في الفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: استفعلت and verbs on its pattern form their verbal nouns on استفعال, as in استخرجت استخراجا and استصعبت استصعابا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: فأما استفعلت فالمصدر عليه الاستفعال وكذلك ما كان على زنته

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: فعلت normally has the verbal noun تفعيل: its initial ت replaces the extra عين in the verb, and its ي corresponds to the alif in إفعال.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: وأما فعلت فالمصدر منه على التفعيل جعلوا التاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: تفعلت has the verbal noun التفعل, preserving the verb’s letters and using a damma on عين; this avoids confusion with تفعيل and needs no added ي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: وأما مصدر تفعلت فإنه التفعل جاءوا فيه بجميع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: Speakers who say كذابا also say تحملت تحمالا, extending the إفعال-like pattern with an alif while retaining all the letters.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: The fixed verbal noun for فاعلت is مفاعلة: its م and ة compensate for two alifs, as in جالسته مجالسة and قاعدته مقاعدة; the source is treated like a passive object.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: المصدر منه الذي لا ينكسر أبدا مفاعلة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: Some use forms such as قيتالا, مراء, and قتالا, preserving more letters and analogizing to إفعال; فعال is common, while مفاعلة remains the regular fixed form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: وأما الذين قالوا تحملت تحمالا فإنهم يقولون قاتلت قيتالا فيوفرون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.claim: تفاعلت takes the source تفاعل, parallel to تفعلت taking تفعل; it is related to فاعلت as تفعلت is to فعلت, and its عين is damma to avoid resemblance to a plural.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمصادرمالحقتهالزوائدمنالف.anchor: ولم يفتحوا لأنه ليس في الكلام

NAHHAS:v5p39/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p39/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p39/r6.claim: The word is explained as burial, and the following إخراجا is the raising for resurrection.

ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.claim: The Meccan surah is devoted entirely to Noah's preaching to his erring people.
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r1.anchor: DEVOTED in its entirety to Noah's preaching to his erring fellow-men

ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.claim: The story symbolically portrays every conscious believer's struggle against blind materialism and the resulting loss of spiritual values.
ASAD-NOTES:71:intro/r2.anchor: symbolically every conscious believer's struggle against blind materialism and the resulting lack of all spiritual values

ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r2.claim: After death God returns people to the earth and then brings them forth in resurrection.
ASAD-NOTES:71:17/r2.anchor: thereafter He will return you to it [in death]

ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:71:17#n11/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase as a final bringing-forth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.claim: Although the six verses could be read as part of Noah’s speech, Islahi prefers to see them as divine insertions; verse 21’s renewed ‘Noah said, My Lord’ marks the transition back to his prayer.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p496/r1.anchor: it seems to me that these are insertions from the Almighty in order to complete Noah’s speech.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.claim: The passage turns from signs in the heavens to signs on earth, presenting humanity first as earth’s noblest creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r5.anchor: attention is directed at the signs of the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.claim: God grew humans from earth, returns them to it at death, and will bring them out of it again.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r6.anchor: the Almighty has grown them from the earth and later, to the earth He returns them and then He will bring them forth from it one day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquence makes the claim itself a clear proof: as vegetation grows, dies, and returns to earth, people do likewise; God’s revival of dead vegetation demonstrates His ability to resurrect people at will.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r7.anchor: just as vegetation sprouts from the earth, the Almighty has grown man from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.claim: The verbal nouns emphasize their respective verbs, but by different modes of emphasis that are difficult to render in translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r8.anchor: are meant to emphasize their respective verbs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r10.claim: For the second verbal construction, Islahi prefers the sense of ease, while allowing other interpretations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p497/r10.anchor: I have preferred the meaning of ease for similar reasons; however, other interpretations are also possible.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r11.claim: God returns people to the earth by making them buried in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r11.anchor: ثم يعيدكم فيها: أي يصيركم فيها مقبورين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r12.claim: God brings people out on Resurrection Day; the verbal noun emphatically asserts that this will certainly happen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p283/r12.anchor: ويخرجكم إخراجا: أي يوم القيامة، وأكده بالمصدر، أي ذلك واقع لا محالة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r1.claim: God returns people to the earth by burying them when they die.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r1.anchor: أي في الأرض بالدفن عند موتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r2.claim: God brings them out of the earth at resurrection and gathering, and the emphatic wording marks this as certain.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r3.claim: Thumma marks the long interval between creation and return, during which people are charged with obligations and earn recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r3.anchor: وعطف يعيدكم بثم لما بين الإنشاء والإعادة من الزمان المتراخي الواقع فيه التكليف الذي به استحقوا الجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r4.claim: Wāw links return and emergence because the states of the barzakh and afterlife form one unit; the whole sequence is certain even if delayed from origination.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p75#4/r4.anchor: لأن أحوال البرزخ والآخرة في حكم شيء واحد فكأنه قضية واحدة ولا يجوز أن يكون بعضها محقق لوقوع دون بعض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r5.claim: God returns people to earth after death and brings them out alive for resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p231#2/r5.anchor: ثم يعيدكم فيها} بعد الموت {ويخرجكم} منها يوم البعث أحياء {إخراجا}

BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r5.claim: Returning people to earth means burying them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r5.anchor: ثم يعيدكم فيها } مقبورين. { ويخرجكم إخراجا

BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r6.claim: Bringing people out means resurrection at the gathering.

BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r7.claim: The verbal noun intensifies the promise, making return as certain as initial creation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:71:15-19/r7.anchor: وأكده بالمصدر كما أكد به الأول دلالة على أن الإعادة محققة كالابداء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.claim: The sūra's aim is to show God's complete power to destroy those warned and replace them with better people, and to bring about the Resurrection that they deny; Noah's story establishes the threat through his people's destruction for rejecting him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على تمام القدرة على ما أنذر به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.claim: The basmala describes God as wholly perfect in majesty and generosity, universally giving outward blessings as al-Raḥmān, and granting His obedient allies lasting blessing as al-Raḥīm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p162#s071/r2.anchor: الذي له الكمال كله من الجلال والإكرام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r11.claim: Returning people to earth is gradual, through death and burial, even if their lifespans are long; death is accepted and undisputed, unlike the disputed initial creation argument.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r11.anchor: الأرض بالموت والإقبار وإن طالت الآجال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r12.claim: God brings people out of the earth through resurrection; the verbal noun following the verb stresses the care taken to ensure its occurrence because they deny it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p171/r12.anchor: بالمصدر الجاري على الفعل إشارة إلى شدة العناية به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.claim: The passage teaches that humans are formed from earth's elements like plants and embeds the promise of life after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r2.anchor: وأدمج في ذلك تعليمهم بأن الإنسان مخلوق من عناصر الأرض مثل النبات وإعلامهم بأن بعد الموت حياة أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r7.claim: إخراجا is kept instead of خروجا because its ending matches the earlier فواصل; preserving such rhyme is a mark of excellence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r7.anchor: بخلاف قوله بعده { إخراجا } فإنه لم يعدل عنه إلى : خروجا ، لعدم ملاءمته لألفاظ الفواصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r8.claim: The resurrection warning is more important than the creation proof, so ثم signals rank rather than time; reburial prepares for the main point, being raised.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r8.anchor: ولكونه أهم رتبة من الاستدلال عليهم بأصل الإنشاء عطفت الجملة ب { ثم } الدالة على التراخي الرتبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r9.claim: The emphatic verbal object reinforces the assertion that God will raise them, answering those who deny resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p204/r9.anchor: وأكد { يخرجكم } بالمفعول المطلق لرد إنكارهم البعث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r19.claim: Returning to the earth means burial, the customary human practice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r19.anchor: والإعادة فيها: هي بالدفن فيها الذي هو عرف البشر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r20.claim: Being brought out means resurrection for the gathering, judgment, and recompense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p374#2/r20.anchor: والإخراج: هو البعث يوم القيامة لموقف العرض والجزاء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r2.claim: God returns people to the earth when they die, then raises them on Judgment Day as He first created them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r2.anchor: أي: إذا متم {ويخرجكم إخراجا} أي: يوم القيامة يعيدكم كما بدأكم أول مرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.claim: Noah invokes God's creative power and greatness and His heavenly and earthly benefits: God provides, made the sky a structure and earth a resting place, and expanded provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r4.anchor: وكل هذا مما ينبههم به نوح، عليه السلام على قدرة الله وعظمته في خلق السموات والأرض، ونعمه عليهم فيما جعل لهم من المنافع السماوية والأرضية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.claim: Because God alone creates and provides without peer, equal, partner, spouse, child, minister, or adviser, He alone must be worshipped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p234/r5.anchor: فهو الذي يجب أن يعبد ويوحد ولا يشرك به أحد؛ لأنه لا نظير له ولا عديل (3) له، ولا ند ولا كفء

JISHUMI:v10p7097/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r12.claim: فجاج are broad, branching roads; a فج can also be a pass between two mountains.
JISHUMI:v10p7097/r12.anchor: والفجاج: الطرق المتسعة المتفرقة، واحدها: فج، وقيل: الفج: المسلك بين الجبلين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r26.claim: God returns people to the earth as corpses in their graves.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p101/r27.claim: God brings people out through resurrection.

BURSEVI:v10p137/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p137/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p137/r10.claim: God returns people to the earth by burial at death, then certainly brings them out at resurrection for the reward of friends and reckoning of enemies.
BURSEVI:v10p137/r10.anchor: أي في الأرض بالدفن عند موتكم {ويخرجكم} منها عند البعث والحشر

BURSEVI:v10p137/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p137/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p137/r11.claim: The conjunction waw joins emergence to return in the grave, signaling that burial and resurrection form one certain sequence, neither part of which can fail.
BURSEVI:v10p137/r11.anchor: ولم يقل ثم يخرجكم بل ذكر بالواو الجامعة إياها مع يعيدكم رمزا إلى أن الإخراج مع الإعادة في القبر

MUQATIL:71:15-20/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r5.claim: After death, people are returned to the earth.

MUQATIL:71:15-20/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r6.claim: At the final blast God brings people out of the earth alive, and to him they return.
MUQATIL:71:15-20/r6.anchor: منها عند النفخة الآخرة { إخراجا } [آية: 18] أحياء وإليه ترجعون

NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r1.claim: God returns people to the earth after death, then brings them out on Resurrection Day.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r1.anchor: بعد الموت ﴿ ويخرجكم ﴾ يوم القيامة ﴿ إخراجا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p284#2/r2.claim: The verbal noun emphatically confirms the act of bringing them out.

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r7.claim: Returning people to the earth refers to burial when they die.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r7.anchor: { ثم يعيدكم فيها } أي عند موتكم بالدفن

QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r8.claim: Bringing people out of the earth refers to resurrection on the Day of Rising.
QURTUBI-FULL:71:17-18/r8.anchor: { ويخرجكم إخراجا } بالنشور للبعث يوم القيامة

QASHANI:71:15-20/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:71:15-20/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:71:15-20/r5.claim: Returning to earth means inclining toward it, taking on its pleasures and desires, and acquiring bodily dispositions and material veils.
QASHANI:71:15-20/r5.anchor: بميلكم إليها وتلبسكم بشهواتها ولذاتها وبهيئات نفوسكم الجسمانية وغواشيكم الهيولانية

QASHANI:71:15-20/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:71:15-20/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:71:15-20/r6.claim: Being brought forth is resurrection from that earth at the station of the heart through voluntary death.
QASHANI:71:15-20/r6.anchor: بالبعث منه في مقام القلب عند الموت الإرادي

RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.claim: The growth of people from the earth, their return to it, and their emergence again form the third proof of God's oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124/r1.anchor: الدليل الثالث : على التوحيد قوله تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r6.claim: The familiar Qur'anic argument is that the One able to create initially is able to resurrect afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r6.anchor: لما كان قادرا على الابتداء كان قادرا على الإعادة

RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r7.claim: The verbal noun intensifies the assertion: God will certainly bring people out again.
RAZI-FULL:v30p124#2/r7.anchor: كأنه قال : يخرجكم حقا لا محالة

STUDYQURAN:71:10/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r16.claim: If verse 14 concerns only life’s stages, this verse extends them through death and resurrection, as in 2:28.
STUDYQURAN:71:10/r16.anchor: When v. 14 is read as referring only to the stages of existence during this life, this verse would complete it

TABATABAI:71:18-24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r1.claim: Returning people to Earth means death and burial; bringing them out means resurrection for judgment.
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r1.anchor: الإعادة فيها بالإماتة والإقبار، والإخراج للجزاء يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:71:18-24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r2.claim: The waw rather than ثم before bringing people out hints that burial and emergence form one process, with return preceding emergence.
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r2.anchor: إيماء إلى أن الاعادة والإخراج كالصنع الواحد

TABATABAI:71:18-24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r3.claim: People are in the abode of truth during their return and emergence, just as worldly life is the abode of delusion.
TABATABAI:71:18-24/r3.anchor: والانسان في حالتي الاعادة والإخراج في دار الحق كما أنه في الدنيا في دار الغرور

TABRISI:71:15-17/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:15-17/r10.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:71:15-17/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives diyar from dawran, with the original form's waw turned into yāʾ and assimilated; ma bi-d-dar diyar means nobody is there moving about.
TABRISI:71:15-17/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج يقال ما بالدار ديار أي ما بها أحد يدور في الأرض

TABRISI:71:15-17/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:15-17/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:15-17/r11.claim: A poet's line uses the connected diyar where separated wording would ordinarily be expected, for poetic necessity.

TABRISI:71:18-23/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:18-23/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:18-23/r3.claim: God returns people to earth as corpses and brings them out alive at resurrection; the verbal noun emphasizes the act of bringing out.

TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.claim: These favors show that God alone deserves worship without association, knows people's interests, and wisely governs them; people should not answer His blessings with disbelief and denial.
TABRISI:71:18-23/r7.anchor: وإنما عدد سبحانه هذه الضروب من النعم امتنانا على خلقه وتنبيها لهم على استحقاقه للعبادة خالصة من كل شرك

THALABI:v10p44#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p44#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p44#2/r10.claim: God returns people into the earth dead and brings them out alive at resurrection.
THALABI:v10p44#2/r10.anchor: ثم يعيدكم فيها أمواتا ويخرجكم منها أحياء إخراجا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r5.claim: God returns people to the earth dead and then brings them out of it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:71:15-18/r5.anchor: ثم يعيدكم فيها } أمواتا { ويخرجكم } منها إخراجا.

ELMALILI:71:17-20/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r9.claim: After indicating the beginnings of human stages, the passage turns to their future and end: return to the earth and subsequent emergence from it.
ELMALILI:71:17-20/r9.anchor: etvârın mebâdîsine işaretten sonra istikbâlini ve gayesini beyan için de buyuruluyor ki

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r3.claim: Return to the soil and emergence from it again remind people not to forget their responsibility in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:71:17/r3.anchor: insanın, bedeniyle ait olduğu toprağa geri gönderileceği, ancak bir defa daha topraktan hayat alanına çıkarılacağı bildirilerek uhrevî sorumluluğunu unutmaması gerektiğine işaret edilmiştir

BURHAN:v2p393/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r2.claim: إخراجا clarifies that the very people returned to the earth are brought out again, countering the idea that only disembodied souls will be resurrected.
BURHAN:v2p393/r2.anchor: ففائدة ﴿ إخراجا ﴾ ان المعاد في الأرض هو الذي يخرجكم منها بعينه دفعا لتوهم من يتوهم ان المخرج منها امثالهم

BURHAN:v2p393/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r4.claim: The object of أسررت is omitted and understood as supplication, warning, and the like; source-like emphasis can coexist with this ellipsis because the source form is not always used for literal emphasis.
BURHAN:v2p393/r4.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم إني أعلنت لهم وأسررت لهم إسرارا ﴾ فمفعول اسررت محذوف أي الدعاء والانذار ونحوه

BURHAN:v2p393/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r5.claim: Two explanations reconcile إسرارا with the omitted object: it supplies a rhyme rather than emphasis, or أسررت is treated as intransitive after its object is disregarded, like ‘he gives and withholds.’
BURHAN:v2p393/r5.anchor: فان قلت التأكيد ينافي الحذف فالجواب من وجهين أحدهما أن المصدر لم يؤت به هنا للتاكيد وان كان بصورته لان المعنى ليس على ذلك

BURHAN:v2p393/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p393/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p393/r6.claim: Emphasis may use a synonym rather than the verb’s own source: جهارا is a kind of الدعاء, ليا a kind of distortion, and perhaps بهتانا a kind of wrongdoing.
BURHAN:v2p393/r6.anchor: ثم التأكيد بالمصدر تارة يجيء من لفظ الفعل كما سبق وتارة يجئ من مرادفه كقوله تعالى ﴿ إني دعوتهم جهارا ﴾
